images.caption: Figure 1:CADFather overview. Given a target mesh and feedback from existing CAD candidates, the visual assistant selects candidate programs to continue, tools to apply, and the number of proposals to generate. Learned and algorithmic proposals create alternative continuations, while parameter optimization refines existing candidates. The resulting programs are executed and evaluated, and the assistant visually accepts or rejects them before pool admission. Their renders and scores inform subsequent decisions.*In the figures, “stepwise” denotes learned proposals, and “deterministic” or “det” denotes algorithmic proposals.

Figure 2:One assistant decision step: step 3 of the trajectory in Fig.3(MCB chain link). The best candidate c13 has one plate and one post, while the target has two of each. The assistant continues c13 with learned proposal generation and algorithmic proposals; learned proposal generation adds the second post (c15), and the results of both calls enter the transcript of the next step. Abridged from the logged prompt and answer: the rules are paraphrased, the transcript and the rationale are excerpts, the table shows 5 of 10 rows, det denotes algorithmic proposals, and one of four rendered views is shown.

Figure 3:A reconstruction trajectory on an MCB part (a chain link). The figure follows the lineage of the final result, one column per assistant step or group of steps: above each render are the tools called in those steps, with the tool that produced the shown candidate in bold; below it are the candidate ID, IoU, and GMS. The algorithmic start c5 recovers one post, a warm algorithmic proposal adds the lower plate (c13), and learned operation proposals add the second post (c15) and the upper plate (c20); in the same steps the first operations proposed by the learned tool produce only open shells, and the other children score lower. In steps 5–6 the gains become small; the candidate c26 from step 7 has a higher IoU but a lower GMS than c25, and in step 8 the assistant ends the part withfinish(stalled), and the output is the protected best c25.

Figure 5:Examples from the ablation subsets. Each row is one part: the target (GT) and the final results of the full configuration, learned only, w/o algorithmic proposals (w/o det), and w/o optimization, rendered in a common frame. Above each result are its score (Eq.2; zero for an invalid prediction) and the number of tool calls on the lineage of that result (det counts both algorithmic entry points).

Figure 6:Comparison with CADENA, CADFit, and two frontier coding agents. Each row is one part: the target, CADFather (Ours), CADENA-RL, CADFit†, and the reconstructions of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The frontier agents wrote CadQuery code with access to the target mesh and received the score against the target after every attempt.

Figure 7:Failure cases from the full test sets. Each pair shows the target and the CADFather result in a common frame, with IoU and GMS above the result. Left: high IoU with low GMS, where the volume is matched but the knurl (MCB) and the shallow pockets (Fusion360) are missing. Right: parts stopped by the wall-time limit (MCB, a spring reconstructed as a tube) and by the execution limit (Fusion360, a bracket with incomplete ribs).
